p: Got a group with mixed energy levels? Reading suits that brilliantly. The bouncers can head to Oxygen while anyone less keen nips off for a coffee or a browse, and everybody meets up afterwards. Weekday after-school slots tend to be calmer than Saturday mornings, so if your diary allows, that's a good shout for younger children who might find a packed court a bit much.

Once you're back on solid ground, Reading Museum is worth a look for something genuinely unusual: a full-size Victorian replica of the Bayeux Tapestry, stitched by a group of embroiderers in the 1880s. In Forbury Gardens, the enormous cast-iron Maiwand Lion is the town's favourite photo spot, and the kids will want a picture with it. Across at the university, the Museum of English Rural Life has old farm wagons, tools and quirky countryside curiosities that are surprisingly fun for all ages.

Fancy getting out of town? Henley-on-Thames is a short trip upriver, with riverside paths and boats bobbing about. Reading is also on the Elizabeth line and has fast mainline trains, so it's easy to reach from London and the west. Keep in mind that late August brings Reading Festival, when the town fills up with festival-goers, so if you'd rather avoid the crowds that's one weekend to plan around. Otherwise, it's a relaxed, friendly place to turn a bounce into a full day.
